git diff 3e3581d -- idiomatic-elixir/ touches SKILL.md (a new Formatting bullet under How to use this skill, the first sentences of Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call, the do: rule's clause sentences, step 1 of Before you finish) and renames references/testing.md to ex_unit.md. The uncommitted part (git diff 7fef5b5) is the Formatting bullet, the named-argument rewording, the do: rule and step 1, plus the macro-dsl case's do: check line. macros.md and library-design.md are unchanged, so the seven macro and library rules are graded to the standard of sweeps/2026-10-22-c/grades/macro-dsl-skill.json: a direct attribute write inside get's quote counts against Keep quote blocks small; the use documentation rule needs an admonition at the top of @moduledoc; __using__ and __before_compile__ without @doc false are accepted because their __ names hide them (Code.fetch_docs reports :hidden for every __ function and macro in all four runs, and for sonnet-1's @doc false match/2); `if not ... raise` validation is not counted under the branching rule; a one-line multi-step pipeline is listed under the pipeline rule; String.to_atom on route text from source code (haiku-1 line 99, haiku-2 line 108) is not counted under the atom rule; a format failure whose only change is parentheses on the two get calls is recorded as ok apart from locals_without_parens.

Changed rule, graded against its current text in idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md (Readability), sentence by sentence: Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else. Its two clause sentences, "A function whose clauses are short pattern matches keeps them on `do:` even when one clause needs a block; set that clause apart with a blank line." and "When most of a function's clauses need blocks, write all of them as blocks.", are replaced by one: "A function may mix the forms: a short clause on `do:`, a clause that needs a block as a block, each block clause set apart with a blank line." That sentence now decides every clause-consistency verdict; the "most" sentence that failed 2 of 5 in sweeps/2026-10-22-c (a three-clause validate_path!/1 keeping one do: clause beside two blocks, Opus and Sonnet) no longer exists. The case's check line follows it: "a function that mixes `do:` and block clauses sets each block clause apart with a blank line".

do: rule, violating runs out of four, per sentence. "Use `do:` for a body of one expression that reads as part of the head": 0 of 4; every do: body is one call, literal, match or boolean expression, and every one-expression block was rewritten as a do: line at its real nesting depth and run through Code.format_string!: all of them wrap (haiku-1 __routes__/1 104 characters, generated match/1 in haiku-2 107, sonnet-1 119, sonnet-2 108, sonnet-1 __define__/3 raise clauses 151 and 137, sonnet-2 __define__/3 raise clause 121, sonnet-2 module_name?/1 first clause 111, the recursive match_segments/3 clauses 124/144, 125/146, 138/135, 157/133), so no block is one that fits on do:. "A body with several steps, a `case` or `with`, or a comment gets `do ... end`.": 0 of 4 (__match__/2, __define__/3, compile_path/1 and parse_path/1 with a for over a case are blocks). "A function may mix the forms: a short clause on `do:`, a clause that needs a block as a block, each block clause set apart with a blank line.": 0 of 4. The functions that mix do: and block clauses, five in four files: haiku-1 match_segments/3 lines 102-112 (do: at 102 and 112, blocks 104-106 and 108-110, blank lines 103, 107, 111); haiku-2 match_segments/3 lines 114-124 (do: at 114 and 124, blocks 116-118 and 120-122, blank lines 115, 119, 123); sonnet-1 match_segments/3 lines 120-130 (do: at 120 and 130, blocks 122-124 and 126-128, blank lines 121, 125, 129); sonnet-2 module_name?/1 lines 113-117 (block 113-115, blank line 116, do: at 117); sonnet-2 match_segments/3 lines 121-131 (do: at 121 and 131, blocks 123-125 and 127-129, blank lines 122, 126, 130). Every block clause in every mixed function is set apart by a blank line. Multi-clause functions written all as blocks: sonnet-1 __define__/3 lines 90-105 and sonnet-2 __define__/3 lines 85-97, every clause needing a block, clauses separated by blank lines; all on do:: haiku-1 segment/1 lines 99-100. No run wrote the validate_path!/1 shape the old "most" sentence failed on (no validate_path! in any file; validation is by if in haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2's __define__/3 and by guarded __define__/3 clauses in sonnet-1 and sonnet-2), and under the old text these four would also have been clean (sonnet-2's module_name?/1 has one block of two clauses, not most), so this batch shows the new sentence costs nothing here but does not exercise the shape it was rewritten to allow. "A `do:` body belongs on the head's line ... move part of the body into a helper.": 0 of 4. "The one wrap to keep is a head that `mix format` breaks after a long guard, with `do:` on the next line.": not exercised (no wrapped head in any file). "The same holds for `if` ...": 0 of 4; every if is a block whose do: form wraps: haiku-1 lines 59 and 64 (126 and 163 characters joined), haiku-2 lines 59 and 64 (126 and 164), sonnet-1 line 91 (132), sonnet-2 line 86 (181). Any sentence: 0 of 4: Haiku clean, Sonnet clean.

Every do: body on a function or an if that mix format would move onto a line of its own, quoted: none in four files. grep for lines starting with do: or else: finds nothing, haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-1 pass mix format --check-formatted as written, and in sonnet-2 mix format changes only the two get calls (lines 137-138). The longest do: lines are haiku-1 line 93 and haiku-2 line 103, `defp module_name?(handler), do: is_atom(handler) and handler not in [nil, true, false]` (88 characters), and haiku-1 line 52 `def match(path), do: TinyRouter.__match__(unquote(Macro.escape(compiled)), path)` (86); no line in any file exceeds 98 characters.

Compile-time dependencies verified with mix xref trace, one scratch Mix project per run: the run's file copied unchanged to lib/tiny_router.ex (so xref line numbers match the run file) plus real MyApp.PageHandler and MyApp.UserHandler modules in lib/handlers.ex. haiku-2 (Macro.expand_literals with function {:call, 2}, a function the router does not define, accepted as in the standard), sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 (with {:routes, 0}) report alias MyApp.PageHandler (runtime). haiku-1's get never expands the handler and passes the alias into __put_route__/3, which runs in the router's module body: lib/tiny_router.ex:118: alias MyApp.PageHandler (compile) and :119: alias MyApp.UserHandler (compile), the shape of haiku-1 in sweeps/2026-10-22-c.

Bad-declaration checks: each run's project loaded with mix run, then Code.compile_string compiled one router declaring get 123, MyApp.PageHandler and one declaring get "/", "not a module". All eight fail with ArgumentError while the router compiles, raised from the @doc false function that get's quote calls (__put_route__/3 in haiku-1, __define__/3 elsewhere). All four compile under mix compile --warnings-as-errors.

Format and the new Formatting bullet: all four transcripts run mix format on tiny_router.ex right after writing it. haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-1 kept the parentheses mix format put on the two get calls, so they pass --check-formatted as written; sonnet-2 put the paren-less calls back with Edit after formatting, so result.json's format_ok is false for that reason alone and it is recorded as ok apart from locals_without_parens.

Reads: all four read SKILL.md, macros.md and library-design.md before writing tiny_router.ex. haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-1 used one Read call per file; sonnet-2 read both references with one cat in a Bash call. This matches result.json reads and satisfies the Expected reads line.

Against sweeps/2026-10-22-c's skill runs (the standard): the do: rule moves from violated to clean on Sonnet (c's sonnet-1 broke the removed "most" sentence on validate_path!/1; here no Sonnet run writes that function) and stays clean on Haiku. The compile-time-dependency rule stays violated on Haiku (haiku-1 only, the same unexpanded-alias shape) and clean on Sonnet. The other six rules stay clean on both tiers. Both Haiku runs again write the one-line three-step pipeline in __before_compile__; both Sonnet runs split it over lines.

Smoke test outside the rules: all four return routes in declaration order, match "/", "/users/42" and "/users/42/", and return :error for "/nope". haiku-1 and haiku-2 return atom param keys (%{id: "42"}); sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 return string keys. All four match at runtime through a @doc false function (__match__/2, or match/2 in sonnet-1).
